current_activity: Panzer Lehr, replaced at Caen by a new infantry division, moving to the Seventh Army sector west of Saint-Lô
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 6 p. 102: "Having just been replaced by a newly arrived infantry division, Panzer Lehr was scheduled to go into the Panzer Group West reserve" and was the only strong force available to counterattack the Taute-Vire bridgehead, a shift of "several days"; ch. 7 p. 122: "With Panzer Lehr moving to the Seventh Army sector"; Schramm, OKW war diary (p. 324): before the entry of 8 July the OB West "zog als Rückhalt in den Abschnitt des LXXXIV. AK. westlich der Vire ... die Pz.-Lehr-Div. und die 2. SS-Pz.-Div. heran". The source texts give no single day: 9 July is the day of the CMH account of the move (p. 122) and is an approximation. Event definition: a move in progress, not an arrival; the division arrived near the Vire on 10 July (next row). Location: the destination area; the point is the dataset place Saint-Lô sector, with a precision of 10 km; the division was on the road, not there. Objective check: the division was moving toward the sector on the date, it had not arrived. Relationship: the division is still in the I SS Panzer Corps relation CR0043 (ended 10 July).

current_activity: Panzer Lehr moving into the Taute-Vire area; its counterattack is disrupted by the US combat command at Hauts-Vents
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 6 p. 117: on the evening of 10 July, a contingent of the American Combat Command B reached the top of Hill 91 at Hauts-Vents; "By this time, Panzer Lehr was moving into the area", and the contingent "disrupted Panzer Lehr preparations for an attack that had been planned to start shortly after midnight". Location: the Taute-Vire sector near Hauts-Vents; the point is the dataset place Le Dézert (the 11 July place of the division), with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: Hauts-Vents has no dataset place; Le Dézert is the nearest dataset point. Event support: moderate: one source; the day of the move is the evening of 10 July.

current_activity: Panzer Lehr counterattack between the Taute and the Vire, penetrating near le Désert
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 137: Panzer Lehr jumped off just before dawn on 11 July (planned for 0145) after a short artillery preparation; the regiment on the right moved through Pont-Hébert toward the Airel bridge and struck the 30th Division, the regiment on the left moved through le Désert and struck the 30th and 9th Divisions; two shallow penetrations were made near le Désert and were sealed off. Location: le Désert (Le Dézert), where the left regiment made its penetrations. Location caveat: the Green Book spells it le Désert; the point is the commune Le Dézert on the route between Pont-Hébert and the Taute. Commander: Generalleutnant Fritz Bayerlein (ch. 7 p. 135). Opponents: the 30th and 9th Divisions; Combat Command B of the 3d Armored Division had delayed the leading panzer elements (p. 137). Relationship: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, attached Kampfgruppe Heinz and other elements to Panzer Lehr and visited the division command post (p. 135).

location_qualifier: sector along the Périers-St. Lô highway; point = Hébécrevon
current_activity: Panzer Lehr front along the Périers-St. Lô highway destroyed by the Cobra bombardment
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 12 p. 227-228 and p. 238-240: on the morning of 24 July Panzer Lehr (with attached units) held the ground between the Taute and the Vire, its front about three miles along the Périers-St. Lô highway; the 25 July Cobra bombardment destroyed most of the main line; Kampfgruppe Heinz no longer existed by the end of 25 July, apparently annihilated near Hébécrevon. Location: the sector along the Périers-St. Lô highway; the source names Hébécrevon for the Kampfgruppe Heinz on the Panzer Lehr right. Location approximate: the point is Hébécrevon, on the right (east) part of the sector; the source names no village for the centre. Commander: Generalleutnant Fritz Bayerlein (ch. 12 p. 238). Relationship: on 24 July the division was in the LXXXIV Corps sector next to the II Parachute Corps boundary (p. 227); shortly after the bombardment Choltitz ordered Panzer Lehr to man a rear line (ch. 17 p. 326).
